name: Eliam (Bathsheba's father)
title: David's Mighty Warriors
summary: Eliam was the father of Bathsheba, who became King David's wife and the mother of Solomon. He was one of David's thirty mighty men, known for his bravery and loyalty. He was also the son of Ahithophel, David's counselor who later betrayed him during Absalom's rebellion.

keyEvents.title: One of David's Thirty Heroes
keyEvents.description: Eliam is mentioned among David's thirty mighty men, an elite group of warriors who distinguished themselves in battle and loyalty to David.

keyEvents.title: Father of Bathsheba
keyEvents.description: Eliam was the father of Bathsheba, whom David took as his wife after seeing her bathing. This led to one of the most dramatic events in David's life.

keyEvents.title: Son of the counselor Ahithophel
keyEvents.description: As the son of Ahithophel from Giloh, Eliam had close ties to the king's court. Ahithophel's later betrayal of David may have been motivated by David's treatment of his granddaughter Bathsheba.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in Chronicles
keyEvents.description: Eliam is also mentioned in the list of David's mighty men in Chronicles, where he is called Eliam, son of Ahithophel from Giloh.
